page: Amazon Web Services r5b.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU and memory performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 7687.13 and a memory score of 2069.07. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, reaching 376.63 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 44.25 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1282.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1116.0. Similarly, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks fall into the lower performance tier.

This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-core compute speeds or local NVMe storage. The high memory density makes it suitable for database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both perform in the average tier, with Redis achieving 6.89 million operations per second, confirming its suitability for in-memory data stores and transactional databases.
